newsitem.title: INDONESIA: S.Africa's ABSA looks for Asian alliance.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's ABSA looks for Asian alliance.

text.p: South Africa's ABSA bank group considers an alliance with a financial boutique or investment banking operation as the way forward for its business in the Asia-Pacific region, a top ABSA official said on Friday.
"We need somebody with a regional network who can handle the Asian side of international banking deals," ABSA's general manager for the Asia-Pacific region, Louw Burger, said.
"I think what we have concluded in the near term is that the area which needs strengthening is the corporate finance, joint venture and securities business," he told Reuters in an interview.
There were serious problems in trying to build up its own network in the region, he said.
"For us the answer lies in the near term in the form of an alliance with a regional merchant banking, corporate financing, investment banking boutique," he said.
He did not disclose whether any such alliance was imminent.
ABSA -- Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Limited -- established a wholly-owned subsidiary in Hong Kong in 1982. Now known as ABSA Asia Ltd, it operates with a restricted banking licence.

The bank, the biggest in South Africa, established a branch in Singapore on March 31, 1995, as ABSA Bank Ltd with an offshore banking licence. It also opened a representative office in Shanghai in September last year.
Burger described the Singapore and Hong Kong operations as the pillars for the bank's strategy in Asia, with Hong Kong handling China and north Asia, and Singapore handling Southeast Asia.
He said however ABSA had no ambition at present to establish a global banking operation.

"The driving force behind our expanding abroad is not to become some sort of quasi-global bank or even a regional bank outside (South Africa), but really to be able to service the overseas business needs of South African companies and to lead and capture overseas business interests inward into South Africa," he said.

Burger said ABSA had identified three streams of business in which its customers were involved: commercial trade, seeking industrial investment and joint ventures, and investment in South Africa's financial markets.
He stressed the importance of Asia and its huge financial resources for South Africa and the need to develop that market.
"The securities business...is as important as the corporate finance, as important as the trade services because it is the business of tomorrow.

"In 10 years time when ABSA bank does an international rights issue...we're going to be placing that rights issue at the same time in London, in New York, in Frankfurt and also probably in Singapore, or Hong Kong, even Tokyo, so we have to develop those three legs to the stool."

Asked whether ABSA was concerned about its position in Hong Kong with the colony's reversion next year to China and the lack of diplomatic relations between Pretoria and Beijing, Burger said he was optimistic there would be no problems.
He said he expected a smooth transition and that ABSA "has been looking at that and has been talking to the Chinese about that.
"China is incredibly pragmatic in its relations when it comes to people they have differences with but about whom they have positive feelings," he said.
